answer: To bid on routing work, an agent must lock collateral and attach a berth-usage receipt: the harbor authority signs one capacity ticket per occupied slip, and only the current holder can reassign it. Extra keys are cheap, but extra slips are not. Each ticket also commits to a cargo assay—an opal lot number and a yarrow weight—so a reused or forged ticket fails when the assay disagrees with the public slip log. Sybil identities therefore buy no extra bid slots; influence scales with scarce, auditable berth time.
